title: Reduce upgrade blast radius: encrypted backups, strict schema-compat checker, preserve terraform plan
author: Maya K. Singh
description: Motivation: Customers running Private installations asked for tighter upgrade guarantees after a recent minor schema drift incident (see SUP-9021). This PR reduces blast radius for control-plane upgrades by: 1) taking an encrypted, verifiable backup of runtime manifests & DB migration plans before any schema migration; 2) persisting a signed migration state + migration plan checksum to the cluster as a non-deletable marker to block accidental downgrades; 3) adding a strict schema-compatibility checker that validates planned SQL migrations against the current DB schema in a dry-run mode; and 4) preserving terraform plan output (tfplan) and upload it to customer object-store with lifecycle rules so we can reproduce the exact infra diff used during upgrade. Summary of changes: - installer/cli: add rpictl upgrade --dry-run and rpictl backup encrypt|verify commands that integrate with customer KMS via KMS_PROVIDER env var - backup job: kubernetes Job template that snapshots manifests, secrets (only metadata+encrypted blob), and runs pg_dump --schema-only for Postgres-backed installs; output is encrypted using AES256-GCM with a per-upgrade ephemeral key wrapped by customer KMS - migration state: create configmap redwood-upgrade-state that records last_successful_migration, migration_checksum, and signer (GPG/KMS) and is created with an immutable annotation to defend accidental deletion - schema checker: a lightweight SQL analyzer that rejects migrations which drop columns currently used by persisted indexes or dependents; runs in CI and as a pre-flight check in rpictl - terraform module: preserve.tf edits to capture tfplan binary and upload to object-store with integrity checksum; add lifecycle rule prevent_destroy on object-store bucket in terraform recommended templates (opt-in) - helm charts: add pre-upgrade hook that invokes the backup Job when enablePreflightBackup=true - smoke tests: e2e integration harness to exercise upgrade dry-run on minikube with embedded objectstore - docs: detailed upgrade playbook (docs/upgrade-playbook.md) and rollback runbook (docs/rollback-playbook.md). Checklist: [x] Add encrypted backup job template [x] CLI commands and KMS integration [x] Persist migration state to cluster [x] Schema compatibility checks + unit tests [x] Terraform plan preservation and integrity uploads [x] Helm hook and docs [x] E2E smoke test. Related: Linear ENG-5982, PM-331. Links: internal runbook: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-5982, incident SUP-9021. Notes: This is opt-in for private installs that have KMS credentials configured; default behavior remains unchanged (no backups if KMS_PROVIDER unset). The migration-state ConfigMap is deliberately designed to be non-recoverable by simple kubectl delete: the installer will refuse upgrades that would change migration_checksum unless --force-unsafe is provided (and logs explicit risk).

review_comments: Jared Lowe (review): Good shape overall. Request: make the KMS_PROVIDER abstraction pluggable for HSM vendors — see inline. Also request a flag to keep unencrypted local copies for air-gapped debugging.
Maya K. Singh (reply): Added KMS_PROVIDER interface with tests; local debug copy flag is now --debug-unencrypted-copy and disabled by default. See installer/cmd/rpictl/backup.go changes.
Priya Ramos (review): Schema checker is strong; request to add an allowlist for very large tables where DROP COLUMN is allowed if a migration plan includes a rewrite step. Commented on checker.go.
Maya K. Singh (reply): Added allowlist via values.upgrade.schemaAllowlist and unit test covering a large-table drop scenario.
Evan Chu (approve): Verified e2e smoke against minikube+minio; CI flake fixed by increasing job timeout; approving to merge.
release_notes: Add optional pre-upgrade encrypted backups (KMS required)
Persist signed migration state in-cluster to block accidental downgrades
Pre-flight schema compatibility checks for SQL migrations
Preserve and upload terraform plan outputs to object-store for reproducibility
rollback_instructions: To rollback to previous release: 1) Ensure you have the encrypted backup bundle (rpictl backup verify --bundle <id>). 2) Decrypt locally with rpictl backup decrypt --bundle <id> --kms-provider <provider>. 3) Restore manifests: kubectl apply -f <manifests> followed by database restore from pg_dump output if structural revert required. 4) If migration-state configmap blocked downgrade, run rpictl upgrade --force-unsafe --reason 'emergency-rollback' and follow on-call approval flow. Note: force-unsafe bypasses downgrade guard and should only be used with validated backups.
